text.content:
There must be an active scene to use the notebook app.

  • Create notebook item

  • You don't need to edit the notebook item directly. Use the notebook app.

  • You can find it on the left side under "Journal Notes". Then have a look at the second row at the bottom. There you find the notebook icon.

  • Drag'N'Drop a notebook item on the notebook app

  • Drag'N'Drop actors directly on this notebook app

The notebook stores it's data scene based. So, if you switch the scene, it could display another notebook item if the other scene got already configured.

Play a little bit around with the notebook app. It's easy and intuitive.

There is also a keybinding to open the notebook: CTL+J

If you want to place a macro in your macro bar, create a macro of type script with the following code:

NotebookApp.getInstance().render(true, { focus: true })
